c5d5103cc6: When did these SDLT rates start?
19663e0583: 1 April 2025, when the nil-rate band returned to £125,000 and first-time buyer relief to £300,000 (on homes up to £500,000). The 5% additional-property surcharge has applied since 31 October 2024.
bfc2f482ad: What if I replace my main home?
71a592eaaa: If you are replacing your only main residence, choose Moving Home. Higher rates can apply temporarily if you still own the old home on completion day; you can then claim a refund if you sell it within three years.
83cbd892bb: Does this cover Scotland or Wales?
ba7c1e40d8: No. Scotland uses LBTT (nil rate £145,000, 8% ADS) and Wales uses LTT (nil rate £225,000, no first-time buyer relief). Use the dedicated calculators linked above.
429c43bc9b: How much stamp duty does a company pay?
6bf3df27c9: Companies and other non-natural persons buying a dwelling for more than £500,000 usually pay a flat 17% of the whole price (19% if non-UK resident). Below that, standard rates plus the 5% surcharge apply. Qualifying businesses can claim relief from the 17% rate.

f29ce12e70: Is stamp duty the same in England, Scotland and Wales?
2f5ff640ab: No. England and Northern Ireland charge Stamp Duty Land Tax. Scotland charges Land and Buildings Transaction Tax. Wales charges Land Transaction Tax. The bands, first-time buyer rules and additional-home rules are different statutes.
6e5ba91767: Which nation is cheapest for a main home?
7b5bd3949a: It depends on the price. At £250,000 a main home is £2,500 in England and Northern Ireland, £2,100 in Scotland and £1,500 in Wales. At £150,000 England and Northern Ireland charge £500, Scotland charges £100 and Wales charges £0. Use the table for the price you are actually paying.
6e962f5744: Do first-time buyers get relief in every nation?
d6f9fb32e1: England and Northern Ireland: nil-rate to £300,000 if the price is £500,000 or less, otherwise no relief. Scotland: nil-rate to £175,000 with no £500,000 cap, saving up to £600. Wales: no separate first-time buyer relief. The Welsh £225,000 nil-rate band is the standard main-rate threshold.
35862ccc68: England and Northern Ireland add 5% of the whole price on top of standard bands. Scotland adds an 8% Additional Dwelling Supplement on the whole price. Wales does not add a flat surcharge. It uses a separate higher-rate table.
31e5cf72be: Does this compare a shop or office?
a014b1b5a1: Yes, for a non-residential freehold or lease premium. On GOV.UK’s £275,000 commercial example England and Northern Ireland charge £3,250, Scotland charges £2,250 and Wales charges £1,500. Revenue Scotland’s £465,000 case is £12,750 in England, £11,750 in Scotland and £11,000 in Wales. A £300,000 premises is £4,500, £3,500 and £2,750. ADS, the English 5% surcharge and first-time buyer relief do not apply. Lease rent is not calculated.
b0d70281f6: Does this replace the nation calculators?
c06352e9de: No. This page answers which statute applies and what each one charges on the same price. The England, Scotland and Wales calculators are the pages that apply one statute in full, including notes those tools already publish.

7e5b369ceb: How UK Property Tax Was Devolved
c8f06adc5d: Stamp Duty Land Tax once applied across Great Britain. The Scotland Act 2012 devolved it, and Land and Buildings Transaction Tax replaced SDLT in Scotland on 1 April 2015, administered by Revenue Scotland.
cf8936af3c: The Wales Act 2014 followed, and Land Transaction Tax — collected by the Welsh Revenue Authority — replaced SDLT in Wales in April 2018. Northern Ireland still uses SDLT, administered by HMRC.
e25f0bfd9b: Why one comparison page, not three copies
a591ad8bdb: The user job here is “what would this price cost in each nation, and which rule actually applies to me?” The nation calculators answer “how much do I pay under the statute that covers my purchase?” Both jobs are real. Publishing a city page for every town would not change the tax. Publishing England, Scotland and Wales separately does, because the statutes differ. This page only exists to put those three answers next to each other.
2bddbde508: England first-time buyer relief is withdrawn entirely above £500,000. Scotland keeps a £175,000 nil-rate band with no price cap. Wales has no first-time buyer relief, so the Wales column does not change for a first-time buyer.
cd6ea8a20b: England adds 5% of the whole price to standard bands. Scotland adds 8% ADS to standard bands and does not also give first-time buyer relief. Wales switches to the higher-rate table instead of adding a flat percent.

e6a7b107be: Think of It Like a Graduate Tax
fd664312f7: UK income-contingent student loans don't work like a mortgage or credit card. What you repay depends only on what you earn above your plan's threshold — never on the balance. If your pay drops below the threshold, repayments stop. Any balance left at the end of the term is written off.
8579dc6a5b: Key point: for many graduates the balance mostly determines whether anything is written off, not what they pay each month.
7be179ccdf: For students starting in England from August 2023 (Plan 5), the write-off period rose from 30 to 40 years and the threshold fell to £25,000, while interest dropped to RPI only — no extra 3%. The result is that many more Plan 5 borrowers are expected to repay in full than on Plan 2.
8342a04ac7: Write-off terms: Plan 1 — 25 years (most loans); Plan 2 — 30 years; Plan 4 — 30 years; Plan 5 — 40 years; postgraduate — 30 years.
03fa7fdbbe: The user job here is “how much will Student Finance take from this UK salary?” The answer is a function of plan × threshold × rate, not of a loan balance and a 10-year term. The US student loan calculator uses standard amortisation. Changing that page to pounds would still be the wrong formula. GOV.UK publishes the bands; this page does not invent them.
a07bd312ff: You repay a percentage of income above the threshold for your plan. Below the threshold the deduction is £0.
